profiles.title: Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker
profiles.subject: Saints

overview.text: The OCA’s hagiographic account remembers Nicholas as archbishop of Myra in Lycia, a compassionate pastor and wonderworker. Its stories connect episcopal teaching with care for the poor, protection of the unjustly condemned, and deliverance of travelers.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraph; accounts of charity, condemned men, and travelers

overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The selected late-fifteenth- or early-sixteenth-century icon, identified with Poland in its file title, presents Nicholas as a bishop holding the Gospel and blessing. Smaller surrounding scenes narrate his life. This narrative border distinguishes it from a simple bust portrait.

sourceRefs.locator: File description and displayed historic reproduction

blocks.reason: Necessary English description of the selected historic artwork and its published object metadata; no new theological interpretation.

blocks.text: The published life tells of secret gifts for three impoverished daughters, rescue of condemned men, and aid at sea. These episodes are received hagiographic traditions. The account also records the transfer of his relics to Bari in 1087.

sourceRefs.locator: Story of the three daughters; deliverance of three condemned men; paragraph beginning Having reached old age

blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The OCA distinguishes Russian icon types rather than reducing all Nicholas images to one pattern: Zaraisk shows a blessing figure with a Gospel, while Mozhaisk shows him holding a sword and a city. The selected panel belongs to the bishop-and-Gospel visual tradition.
